scope.summary: This Indian Standard series prescribes definitions, general requirements, testing methodologies, and individual material specifications for solvent-containing electrical insulating varnishes used for impregnating, finishing, and coating electrical windings, transformers, coils, and electric motors. Part 3, Section 2 specifically covers physical, mechanical, and electrical requirements for hot curing impregnating varnishes across thermal classes 130 to 220.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Specification. However, under public utility contracts (such as state electricity boards—JVVNL, KSEB—and central railway specifications), raw insulating varnishes supplied for winding repair and motor manufacture must be certified to comply with IS 10026 and carry corresponding batch test records.

requirements.detail: Observed or calculated final test values, solid contents, viscosity flow times, or breakdown voltages must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
Measured by heating a 1.5 g liquid specimen at 130°C or 150°C for 2 hours to calculate active dry resin percentage, which must typically range between 45% and 55% to prevent excessive solvent loss.

requirements.requirement_type: Ability to Cure in Thick Layer
requirements.detail: A critical test for impregnating varnishes. Evaluates if the varnish inside a deep winding cavity will cure fully into a solid, bubble-free mass when baked at 120°C for 10 hours.

The cured varnish film must exhibit high dielectric strength, withstanding voltages exceeding 100 kV/mm under ambient conditions, and retaining high dielectric protection after wet conditioning or water immersion.
The cured film must maintain a volume resistivity exceeding 10^15 Ohm-cm under standard ambient conditions, and remain above 10^12 Ohm-cm after 168 hours of water immersion.
Part 3, Section 2 specifies five hot-curing thermal classes: Class 130 (Class B), Class 155 (Class F), Class 180 (Class H), Class 200, and Class 220 based on long-term thermal endurance index limits.
Under active Amendment No. 1 (November 2019), Row 10 of Table 1 (regulating liquid properties) is amended to substitute 'Test method is under consideration' for the older numerical value '22'.
Under active Amendment No. 1 (November 2019), Row 4 of Table 2 (regulating cured film properties) is amended to substitute 'Test method is under consideration' for the older numerical value '23'.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 10026 is the primary national Indian Standard specification governing solvent-containing electrical insulating varnishes used to coat and impregnate motor windings, transformers, and electronic components. Technically aligned with international standards IEC 60464 and IEC 61033, the code is divided into three parts: Part 1 defines vocabulary, Part 2 outlines physical and electrical test methods (such as flow-cup viscosity, closed-cup flash point, dynamic bonding strength, volume resistivity, and thick-layer curing), and Part 3 Section 2 specifies individual material requirements for hot curing impregnating varnishes across thermal classes 130 to 220. Incorporating Amendment No. 1 (November 2019), the standard marks specific properties in Table 1 and Table 2 as 'under consideration' to reflect ongoing technical developments, ensuring high dielectric protection and vibration-damping in national electrical grids.
